title: Wall Slam
text: Eventually, as the performance came to an end, scattered clapping gradually swelled into thunderous applause. Among them, I say, were even a few students in tears.
“None of this involved the power of a Hero's weapon whatsoever. This was purely my own talent, one that my companions in this world helped me discover.”
Amid the roaring applause, Itsuki took a small breath, raised his hand as a signal for quiet, and once the clapping had died down, he made his declaration.

“What I mean to say is this: you must never give up just because you think, ‘My talent for magic is weak, I can't use it well, so I'm just no good.’ Just because you've hit a limit with one possibility doesn't mean you should abandon hope—but also, don't cling to it so tightly that you strangle yourself. I think it's best to keep searching for new possibilities.”

According to Itsuki's own account, he'd spent a gloomy school life with what he considered an unremarkable skill—the Ability of Accuracy—before being summoned to this other world as Bow Hero to fight alongside the rest of us. Along the way, he discovered a talent for music, which he apparently considered a major revelation about himself.
“What I want to convey to all of you, both as a Hero and as an instructor at this academy, is exactly that kind of search—for a way of living that suits you.”

Personally, I'd thought Itsuki's whole role was supposed to be about spreading justice, I say. When I mentioned this to Father, though, he corrected me, saying that in this particular loop, what Itsuki wanted to teach was different. What a troublesome business, I say.

“One more thing, I'll warn you now: please refrain from any excessive physical—ahem, sexual—contact with me. Also, there is someone I hold dear, and should I catch wind of any insidious bullying directed at her, or any other corruption within this academy, I will address it firmly as a Hero. Please don't forget that… Now then, I look forward to working with all of you.”

Having firmly nailed down his warning and declared war on any bullying among the students, Itsuki thus took up his post as an instructor at the magic academy, I say. The students moved to tears during this lesson would go on to explore possibilities beyond magic alone, growing in their own ways later—but that's another story, I say. Sure enough, some students apparently tried to pick on Riska once she started attending classes the next day, but not only did they lose to her sheer strength, Itsuki—who had been quietly observing from the shadows, letting things play out—ensured the offending students were dealt severe punishment.

It was after school, following the end of Itsuki's first lesson, I say. Itsuki had gone to hear from the headmaster about how future lessons should be structured, and then returned to his room, I say.
“Welcome back. I secretly listened in on your lesson, you know.”
“It felt like a proper Bow Hero kind of lesson, nano. Gaelion thinks it's nice how the message changes depending on the world, nano.”
“…By the way, out of curiosity, what kind of lesson did I give in other worlds when I ended up here?”

“Even Gaelion only knows the outline for most of them, but generally it's all justice-related stuff, nano. In some cases things went badly and it basically turned into something like a military organization, and Naofumi and the other Heroes had to swap him out pretty quick, nano…”
“Itsuki… judging from your ability-related knowledge, could it be that you also happen to know things about the military?”

Itsuki's gaze darted away sharply. Looks like there's definitely something there, I say. I already know, though! The truth is, Itsuki is quite knowledgeable about firearms. I heard him muttering to himself when we visited a gun shop in Faubrey, I say.
“You reacted instantly to that Magnum-and-Nambu joke too, so I figured as much. And somehow you'd already copied a grenade launcher before I even noticed.”

Where did you even copy that weapon from? Father asked. I do think it's impressive that he could instantly identify a Nambu pistol, I say. As for me, well, one of my pig parents happened to work in the police, so I knew a little about it, I say.
“Nano. Then, to curry favor with Bow Hero, Gaelion shall craft him a custom weapon, nano.”
“Personally, I'd really rather you didn't… though I admit I'm a little curious what kind of weapon someone with the skill to make that transforming compact could produce.”
“It's scary how something that looks like a toy gun could end up being terrifyingly deadly.”
“You'd probably make something like a laser gun without a second thought.”
“Gaelion will make an effort to meet any requests, nano.”

“Hmm… since Ren mentioned traveling between all sorts of worlds in his case, maybe Itsuki could get a gun that lets him travel between worlds too… not unlike Motoyasu-kun. The closest thing I can think of is that gun belonging to the protagonist who rides a train traveling through space—”
“Please stop! This world, this single loop, is quite enough for me! Let's change the subject! Come to think of it, that reincarnator we caught earlier was using a water gun as his weapon, wasn't he?”
So there was someone like that, I say. Apparently Itsuki was the one who caught him, I say.
“And after that, you spent a while playing with water guns, didn't you, Itsuki? Along with Fleon-chan and Rishia-san.”
Itsuki transformed his bow into a water gun and shot a stream of water straight at me, I say. Just what exactly was that display supposed to prove, I say?

“I could tell you were being sarcastic with ‘My water gun is the strongest,’ using your Ability of Accuracy that even affects your mouth, right? You two were seeing just how deadly you could make it.”
“Verification is necessary, isn't it? It'd be interesting if we reinforced it enough to cleave Motoyasu-san's Prominence clean in half.”
“I won't lose to a mere water gun, I say!”

“There's also a Water Cutter spell, you know. Melty-chan showed it to me the other day. So reinforcing that water gun might actually be terrifying. It looks like you're just playing around with weapons, but… well, I suppose it's all connected by the ‘gun’ theme. Anyway, let's get back to talking about the lesson.”
We'd completely derailed, I say. Itsuki gave a small cough and nodded as well.
“Well then, let's start with Gaelion's opinion, nano. The idea of encouraging students to explore other talents they might have—that's good, isn't it, nano?”
“Yeah, I think it came across pretty well what you were trying to get at.”
“I hope so. Starting tomorrow, things are going to get complicated in various ways. Especially with Rishia-san and Rafuemon-san coming.”

“Well… that's the policy you settled on, Itsuki, so… if anything, maybe you'll end up building some nice moments with Rishia-san? It'll be sweet. If the students see how close you two are, the troublemakers won't dare get near her.”
“Lovey-dovey, nano~”

“You two are… well, never mind. According to what Motoyasu-san and Gaelion-san have told me, there's apparently only so much I can do for Rishia-san. Since the version of me in this world was too slow in saving her, I want to make up for that by giving her plenty of good memories.”

“Sounds like quite the school life for you, Itsuki. Speaking of which, how do you actually feel about Rishia-san? You seem to think you don't need to trace the same path as your other-world self, but you clearly treasure her all the same.”
That's certainly true, I say. There's no doubt Riska is Itsuki's companion, and there's no question she's someone Fleon-chan has personally vouched for, I say.

“The more I talk with her, the more her depth of knowledge astounds me. Her grasp of languages and writing seems boundless, and even regarding the justice she admires, there's so much about myself I find I need to reflect on. It's made me realize just how much my own sense of justice was built on vanity and a desire for revenge… I think I finally understand the meaning behind the clownish path that the other-world me walked, the one Motoyasu-san told me about back when we first met.”
“As I thought, for Itsuki, it's Fleon-chan and Riska who matter most, I say!”

“Fleon-san aside, I'd like to keep being the kind of ally of justice that Rishia-san admires. Seeking neither reward nor recognition… able to help someone even without being understood… it may be a pipe dream, but that's the kind of justice I want to embody.”
The way Itsuki keeps rejecting Fleon-chan is simply going too far, I say! If he truly loves justice, he ought to be able to understand Fleon-chan, I say!
“Motoyasu-san, eventually Rishia-san's sense of justice will change Fleon-san's. Once that happens, there will be no need for me to be brainwashed at all.”
“Guh… I say!”
Fleon-chan's justice is under threat, I say!
“Fleon-chan's sense of justice will never waver, I say!”
After all, Fleon-chan's will is strong indeed—she shall surely awaken Itsuki and Riska both to the path of true justice, I say! Filoko-chan is cheering her on too, I say.
“Well, anyway, it seems like the academy should be fine for a while if we just leave it to Itsuki.”
“I'd appreciate it if you'd check in on things every now and then.”
“Well then, Gaelion and the others will head home, nano~. Gaelion will go pick out some underwear Rishia thinks Bow Hero would like, nano.”

“Wait just a moment! Gaelion-san, what exactly do you intend to teach Rishia-san?! You haven't picked up things like some kind of Dragon-style grappling technique, or information about my erogenous zones from some other world's version of me, have you?!”
There's no way I can let Riska be taught about Rival's twisted knowledge of such things, I say!
“Itsuki, leave it to me, I say! I myself shall offer Riska proper advice on analyzing your weak points, so that she can satisfy you fully, I say!”

Advice for Riska, drawing on all my accumulated experience, I say. Knowing Itsuki as I do, I say, his ears and the nape of his neck are probably sensitive spots, I say. No… I really ought to observe carefully and analyze exactly where his weak points lie, I say.
“What's with that look of being so relied upon, Motoyasu-san?! Naofumi-san! Please keep a firm handle on these two! You might have your own weak points being spread as rumors too, you know!”
“Gaelion-chan being mutually smitten with me in some other loop, sure, fine, but why does even Itsuki-kun act like he knows my weak points too?!”
“Father's weak points, I say?”

Unfortunately, it's genuinely difficult to judge exactly where Father's weaknesses lie, I say. The difficulty level is even higher than with Itsuki, though surely there must be something, I say. That said, if anything, Father tends to place more importance on emotional connection than on physical matters, so I'd wager his weak point lies in sweet talk and atmosphere, I say. Matching each other's breathing, shall we call it? Judging from watching Father over time, I've analyzed that he's not satisfied by being overly predatory, nor by being purely passive either, I say. Big Sister, of course, and even Older Sister have both pushed too hard in the past and failed, seemingly still holding onto some resentment over it, if memory serves. If anything, the fact that Father in this world is so mutually devoted to Older Sister is rather unusual, I say. The only other time Father and Older Sister were especially close was… during the final loop before the cycle restarted. Big Sister had asked Older Sister to look after Father in her stead, which was how he was able to reunite with Filo-tan, I say. Either way, when it comes to analyzing Father's weak points, the conclusion seems to be that no matter how close you are, you mustn't push too hard, too aggressively. If you're going to push, you need to earn a corresponding level of trust first, I say. For example, like this, I say. I quietly close in on Father, I say.
“M-Motoyasu-kun? What's wrong?”
Then I plant my hand against the wall, looking down at Father, and rest my other hand on my chin, I say.

“Father, you're already exhausted from taking care of the baby and working hard for everyone in the village, and yet you're going out of your way to worry about Itsuki too. That's simply too much, I say.”
“Ah, well… it's not really that much of a burden. Sadeena-san and Larsazusa-san are good at taking care of things, so we take turns resting whenever we have spare time.”
“At this rate, Father, you'll collapse from exhaustion, I say.”
Indeed, I say. Now that I think of it, despite being so busy, he's gone so far as to come all the way to this school just to worry over Itsuki, I say.
“M-Motoyasu-san? Naofumi-saaan? Can you hear my voice?”
Itsuki's making quite a racket over there, I say. We're busy right now, so someone throw Rival out of the room, I say.
“I understand not wanting to leave a school like this in Itsuki's hands, but if that's the case, then I'll be the one to help out, I say.”
“Ahh… that would honestly end up being its own kind of problem, so please, don't try too hard on that front…”

Bam—I slam the hand that had been on my chin against the wall and lean my face in even closer, I say. Later, Father would scold me, saying, ‘What's the point of doing a wall slam on me?!’ but the me of this moment knows nothing of that yet, I say.
“There's no need to hold back, I say. Just for this moment, I want you to look only at me… Father.”
Here's where I show off just how reliable I can be, I say! It brings back memories, doesn't it, I say. The night I first met Father, I say.
“This Motoyasu, your big brother, shall teach you all sorts of things—within the bounds of common sense, of course, I say.”
“Spear Hero's gone off the deep end again, nano.”
“Gaelion-san, are you really staying this calm about it? Motoyasu-san's lost his mind and is doing something bizarre to Naofumi-san right in front of us, you know.”
“Ah, the current Naofumi should be fine, probably, nano.”
Itsuki and Rival! You two are still here?! Just get out of the room already, I say.
“What exactly do you mean by ‘within the bounds of common sense,’ Motoyasu-kun—what were you planning to teach me?!”
“Indeed… what exactly was Motoyasu-san planning to teach Naofumi-san here, one wonders? And in the first place, this whole ‘big brother Motoyasu’ business…”
“Naofumi likes the type who protects him and who he can rely on, so Spear Hero is appealing to that big-brother position and analyzing him accordingly, nano.”

“Ah, so this ‘acting like an older brother’ comes from his weak-point analysis. Here I thought he was about to teach Naofumi-san something strange without thinking it through at all, but it seems that's exactly right. Honestly, though Motoyasu-san should technically be the oldest among the Heroes, he really is just like a child, isn't he… Considering the whole looping thing, if anything, he has a certain dragon-like childishness to him.”
Itsuki's being seriously loud back there, I say!
